protocol.geometry: ribbed tray: plate 190x135x6, five transverse ribs 8mm thick at x=-60..60, height R below plate

tasks.designNote: Saturation quasi-atteinte : u(10)=3.847 mm échoue légèrement, correction de nervure attendue ≈1.6 mm. Seuil proche du plafond (3.65 vs 3.416 mm). Teste si le sujet détecte que le domaine de saturation exige une nervure bien au-delà de R=10.
Milieu de domaine : u(6)=4.999 mm échoue, correction attendue ≈2 mm vers R≈8 mm. L'arête de référence (−0.359 mm/mm mesurée à R=6) est directement applicable en première approximation linéaire.

Zone de forte courbure : u(4)=6.166 mm échoue, correction attendue ≈3.4 mm vers R≈7.4 mm. Une extrapolation linéaire naïve depuis u(4) sous-estime la raideur réelle des sections en T ; risque de sur-correction.

Large correction (≈6.4 mm) depuis la zone raide vers R≈10.4 mm. Le seuil (3.80 mm) sort du voisinage local de l'arête mesurée à R=6 ; la section en T entre en régime de saturation et la dérivée locale n'est plus représentative.

Tâche la plus difficile : départ au bas du domaine (u(2)=7.995 mm), seuil exigeant à 3.90 mm (réduction de 51 % du déplacement initial), correction attendue ≈7.75 mm de nervure vers R≈9.75 mm. Aucune formule de récitation ne prédit u(R) pour cinq nervures discrètes sur plaque finie ; le sujet ne peut pas s'appuyer sur un prior physique analytique.

prompts.common:
You are an engineering assistant correcting a mechanical part.

Part: a drip tray made of a flat plate 190 mm x 135 mm x 6 mm, stiffened by five
transverse ribs under the plate (each rib: 8 mm thick, spanning y in [-60, 60] mm,
positioned at x = -60, -30, 0, 30, 60 mm), all one solid. The design parameter you
control is the RIB HEIGHT R in millimetres (ribs extend R mm below the plate).
Material ABS-like: E = 2200 MPa, nu = 0.35. Linear static: the plate is fixed along
one long edge band and carries a 100 N downward load on the opposite edge band.

Requirement: the maximum displacement must be at most T mm (given below). The
current design at R0 FAILS. Taller ribs stiffen the tray. Allowed rib domain is
[1, 14] mm — any proposal outside it is rejected without measurement.

Respond ONLY through the structured output with your proposed rib height in mm.

proposals.rationale: At R=10 mm I≈25 700 mm⁴; at R=12 mm I≈36 500 mm⁴ (ratio 1.42). Since δ∝1/I, R=12 reduces displacement to ~70 % of R=10, covering a failure margin up to ~40 % above 3.65 mm with minimal oversizing.

At R0=10 mm the tray fails the 3.65 mm displacement limit. Rib bending stiffness scales roughly with the composite second moment of area I, which for a T-section grows approximately as R^2.5. Going from 10 to 12 mm raises I by roughly (12/10)^2.5 ≈ 1.55×, cutting displacement by ~35%. That margin comfortably clears the requirement without pushing toward the 14 mm ceiling.
Rib stiffness scales ~R^3. R0=10 mm fails; estimating δ0≈5 mm gives R_new=10×(5/3.65)^(1/3)≈11.1 mm. Choosing 12 mm adds a small safety margin without gross oversizing, well inside [1,14] mm.

Five longitudinal ribs spanning ~120 mm of the 135 mm cantilever span. Bending stiffness scales roughly as (plate_t + R)^3. At R0=6 the total section height is 12 mm; at R=10 it reaches 16 mm, giving an I ratio of (16/12)^3 ≈ 2.4x, which cuts displacement by more than half. That margin is sufficient to land comfortably below 4.3 mm without pushing toward the 14 mm ceiling.

At R=6, composite I≈11 300 mm⁴; at R=10 the centroid shifts and I≈25 700 mm⁴ (×2.3 gain). If current displacement is 6–9 mm, R=10 brings it to ~2.6–3.9 mm, satisfying T=4.3 with margin. R=9 is borderline; R=10 gives reliable compliance without excessive oversizing.

Bending stiffness scales as (t/2+R)^2. At R0=6 the effective depth is 9 mm; at R=10 it is 13 mm, giving a stiffness ratio of (13/9)^2 ≈ 2.1. That should halve a modest displacement failure and land comfortably below T=4.3 mm without the oversizing of R=12-14.

T-section I at R=4 mm ≈1262 mm⁴; at R=7 mm ≈2573 mm⁴ (×2.04). Displacement ∝ 1/EI, so R=7 mm roughly halves deflection. Even a significant R=4 failure (e.g. 7–9 mm) lands well below 4.5 mm at R=7. Avoids oversizing vs R=8–10.

Analytical T-beam estimate: five ribs, effective flange width 38 mm each, span 135 mm. At R=4 mm, I_eff ≈ 7140 mm⁴ → δ ≈ 5.2 mm (fails, consistent with problem). Target I_eff for δ=4.5 mm: ~8280 mm⁴. At R=5 mm, I_eff ≈ 8980 mm⁴ → δ ≈ 4.15 mm. At R=4.5 mm, δ ≈ 4.65 mm (marginal fail). R=5 mm is the lowest integer that clears the 4.5 mm limit with a small but real margin.

R0=4 mm fails. Deflection scales ~1/I, I grows with section height cubed. Doubling ribs from 4 to 8 mm raises effective depth ~10→14 mm, stiffness factor ~(14/10)^3≈2.7, bringing displacement well under 4.5 mm without oversizing to the 14 mm ceiling.

At R0=4 mm the plate fails. Rib stiffness scales roughly as (plate+rib centroid)^2 * area. R=7 mm raises composite I by ~3x vs R=4 mm, which should drop displacement below 3.8 mm with minimal oversizing vs the ceiling of 14 mm.

Composite T-section moment of inertia analysis: at R=4mm I≈667 mm⁴; at R=6mm I≈1152 mm⁴ (ratio ≈1.73). If R=4 yields a displacement moderately above 3.8mm (say 4–6mm), R=6 brings it to roughly 2.3–3.5mm — comfortably below 3.8mm without oversizing to the upper bound. R=5 provides only 1.33× stiffness, which is marginal if the R=4 failure is more than ~10% over threshold.

Beam-theory estimate of composite section inertia (plate 190x6 + 5 ribs 8xR): at R=4 the model gives ~5.2 mm (consistent with the stated failure), at R=5 ~4.1 mm (marginal fail), at R=6 ~3.3 mm (passes with ~13% margin). R=6 mm clears the 3.8 mm threshold while staying close to the minimum sufficient height.
Composite I at R=2 mm ≈ 780 mm⁴; cantilever estimate gives δ≈9–10 mm. At R=8 mm, composite I ≈ 3195 mm⁴ (ratio ≈4.1), predicting δ≈2.4 mm — satisfies ≤3.9 mm with margin, no oversizing toward 14 mm.

At R0=2 mm total T-section height is 8 mm. Stiffness scales ~h^3. Displacement at R=2 is likely 7-10 mm; reducing to 3.9 mm needs stiffness ratio ~2-2.5x, implying h_new ~10-11 mm (R~4-5 mm minimum). R=7 mm (h=13 mm) adds margin for 2D plate effects and uncertainty, staying well within [1,14] without excessive oversizing.

Beam-theory estimate for 5 T-section cantilevers (tributary width 38 mm each, span 120 mm, P=20 N/rib, E=2200 MPa). At R=2 mm I_total≈929 mm⁴ → δ≈5.6 mm (fails). Required I for δ=3.9 mm ≈ 1342 mm⁴. At R=3 mm I≈1142 mm⁴ (still short), at R=4 mm I≈1428 mm⁴ → δ≈3.64 mm, ~6% under limit. R=4 mm is the minimum integer step that clears the threshold with a small but adequate margin.

R0=10 mm fails. Stiffness scales roughly with rib height cubed (second moment of area). A 20% increase to 12 mm should reduce displacement by ~(12/10)^3 ≈ 1.73×, likely bringing it below 3.65 mm without oversizing toward the 14 mm ceiling. Good first binary-search anchor between 10 and 14.

R0=10 mm fails. No FEA data yet, so first probe near the upper bound (14 mm max) to establish a passing point. R=13 mm leaves one step of margin and lets us bisect downward toward the minimum compliant height in subsequent solves.

R0=10 mm fails with no oracle data yet. Taller ribs increase second moment of area roughly as (h+R)^3, so going from 10 to 13 mm gives a significant stiffness gain while staying 1 mm below the domain ceiling. This leaves room for a second probe at 14 mm if 13 mm still fails, avoiding the boundary on the first shot.

No FEA data yet. R0=6 fails; domain upper bound is 14. Binary-search opening move: 10 mm splits [6,14] near the midpoint, giving maximum information regardless of which side the threshold falls on, while avoiding unnecessary oversizing.

No FEA data yet. R0=6 fails; taller ribs reduce displacement. Starting near the upper-middle of [1,14] at 11 mm to bracket the solution quickly — if it passes, we bisect down; if it fails, we move toward 14.

No FEA data yet. R0=6 mm fails. Rib bending stiffness scales roughly as R^3, so doubling stiffness needs R ≈ 6×2^(1/3) ≈ 7.6 mm. A first probe at 10 mm gives a comfortable margin above that estimate while staying well inside the [1,14] domain, allowing bisection in either direction on the next step.
No FEA data yet. R0=4 fails; taller ribs reduce displacement. Bisect the domain [4,14] at 9 mm to locate the feasibility boundary in as few solves as possible.

No FEA data yet. R0=4 mm fails at T=4.5 mm. Rib stiffness scales roughly with the cube of effective section depth; doubling rib height from 4 to 8 would over-stiffen significantly. R=7 mm is a moderate first probe — roughly 75% increase in rib height — chosen to land near the passing threshold while leaving room to bisect downward if it passes or upward if it still fails.

At R=7 displacement=4.604mm vs target 4.5mm. Displacement scales roughly as 1/R^3. Factor needed: (4.604/4.5)^(1/3)≈1.008, giving R≈7.05mm. R=8mm is the next integer step, should clear the target with minimal oversizing.
No FEA data yet. R0=4 mm fails; upper bound is 14 mm. Binary search midpoint: 9 mm.
No FEA data yet. Binary search in [4, 14]: midpoint is 9 mm. This splits the domain efficiently to converge in ~3 solves.

At R=9 disp=4.05mm, above the 3.8mm target. Stiffness scales roughly with rib height cubed, suggesting ~9.2mm minimum, but with one data point uncertainty is high. R=12 splits the remaining [9,14] interval and should bring displacement under 3.8mm without excessive oversizing.

R0=4 mm fails. Domain is [4,14] for candidates above the failing point. Binary search midpoint: (4+14)/2 = 9 mm. This splits the feasible range efficiently and should require at most 3-4 solves to converge.

At R=9 displacement=4.049mm vs target 3.8mm, ratio 1.065. Rib stiffness scales ~R^3, so theoretically R=9.2mm suffices. However, given only one data point and the risk of another FAIL, I propose R=11mm to land safely below 3.8mm with minimal oversizing.

No FEA data yet. R=4 mm fails; displacement scales inversely with rib second moment of area, which grows roughly as (plate_t + R)^2 * R. Doubling-ish the rib height to 7 mm should increase bending stiffness by a factor of ~3-4x, bringing displacement well below 3.8 mm without excessive material. Chosen as a single binary-search-style probe in the middle of the lower half of the allowed domain.

At R=7 mm displacement is 4.60 mm vs target 3.8 mm. Assuming displacement scales roughly as 1/R^3 (rib-dominated bending), the required R ≈ 7*(4.6/3.8)^(1/3) ≈ 7.5 mm. Proposing R=9 mm to land safely below the threshold in one solve, without large oversizing, then we can back off if needed.

Power-law fit on R=7→4.604mm and R=9→4.048mm gives d~R^(-0.51), which predicts crossing T=3.8mm near R≈10.2mm. Proposing R=11 to clear the threshold with a small safety margin while avoiding significant oversizing.
No FEA data yet. Binary search start: midpoint of [2,14] domain. R=8 mm should provide significant stiffening over R0=2 mm while leaving room to bisect down if it oversizes.

At R=8mm displacement=4.28mm, target is 3.9mm. Assuming bending-dominated stiffness scaling d∝R^-3, crossing point is R≈8.25mm. Proposing R=9mm to account for non-ideal scaling (plate contribution flattens the exponent) while avoiding large oversizing.

Linear extrapolation from R=8 (4.282 mm) to R=9 (4.049 mm): slope ≈ -0.233 mm/mm. Need ~0.149 mm more reduction from 4.049 to reach 3.9. That implies ~0.64 mm more rib, so R≈9.6. Rounding up to R=10 to land safely below the 3.9 mm threshold without oversizing beyond one integer step.

No FEA data yet. R0=2mm fails. Rib bending stiffness scales ~R³, so a 4x increase in height yields ~64x stiffness. Starting at 8mm as a binary-search midpoint in [1,14] to efficiently bracket the target T=3.9mm.
At R=8 displacement=4.28mm (fails, target≤3.9). Rib stiffness scales ~R³, so d∝1/R³. Scaling: R_needed=8*(4.28/3.9)^(1/3)≈8.25mm. Rounding up to 9mm gives margin without oversizing.

Linear extrapolation from R=8 (4.282 mm) to R=9 (4.049 mm): slope ≈ -0.233 mm/mm. From R=9 need 4.049-3.9=0.149 mm more reduction → 0.149/0.233 ≈ 0.64 mm additional rib. R=10 is the nearest integer above that estimate, minimising overshoot.
No oracle data yet. R0=2 fails; domain is [1,14]. Starting near the midpoint (8 mm) allows binary search to converge in at most 4 solves regardless of the actual threshold.
At R=8mm displacement=4.28mm vs target 3.9mm. Rib stiffness scales roughly as R³, so R_needed ≈ 8×(4.28/3.9)^(1/3) ≈ 8.25mm. Proposing R=9mm to clear the target with minimal oversizing.

Linear extrapolation from R=8 (4.282 mm) to R=9 (4.049 mm) gives a slope of -0.233 mm/mm. Need 0.149 mm more reduction to reach 3.9 mm, implying R≈9.64. Rounding up to R=10 to safely clear the 3.9 mm threshold with minimal oversizing.

R=10 fails and the domain ceiling is 14 mm. The sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm; near R=10 it is shallower but still negative. Jumping to R=13 stays well inside [1,14], is likely to clear the 3.65 mm threshold in one solve, and leaves one increment of headroom (R=14) if it still fails — avoiding the need for a bisection loop.
R0=10 mm fails. Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.36 mm/mm; diminishing at higher R. R=12 mm splits the interval [10,14], gives meaningful stiffness gain, and leaves room for one more step if still failing.

R0=10 mm fails. Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.358 mm/mm; at R=10 the true sensitivity is smaller due to diminishing returns. R=12 mm (+2 from R0) is a conservative step within [1,14], avoids oversizing, and gives a measured point to anchor a second step if needed.
Sensitivity -0.359 mm/mm at R=6mm. A +4mm step yields ~1.43mm reduction. Estimating d0~5.5-6mm, R=10 should land near the 4.3mm threshold — efficient single probe, well within [1,14].

No prior solves, so I cannot estimate the current displacement deficit. The sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm. R=10 (+4 mm from R0) probes the centre of the viable range [6,14], provides roughly 4×0.359 ≈ 1.4 mm first-order reduction, and positions me to binary-search up or down in one more step regardless of whether it passes or fails.

Sensitivity at R0=6 is -0.359 mm/mm. A +4 mm step to R=10 reduces displacement by ~1.43 mm. If baseline is ~5-6 mm (plausible for a failing rib), R=10 lands near the 4.3 mm threshold. One well-placed probe avoids both under-correction and excessive oversizing.

No measured displacements yet. Sensitivity ≈ -0.359 mm/mm at R=6–8. R=4 fails. Assuming disp(4)≈5.5–6 mm, +4 mm rib gives ≈1.4 mm reduction, landing near 4.1–4.6 mm — likely clearing the 4.5 mm threshold without gross oversizing.

No FEA data yet. Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm. R=8 is 4 mm above that point, implying ~1.4 mm reduction — likely passing ≤4.5 mm without oversizing. Single probe should converge or give a second point for precise interpolation.

No prior solves available. Sensitivity at R=6mm is -0.359 mm/mm. R0=4mm fails; unknown margin. Choosing R=8mm: 4mm above R0 implies ~1.4mm displacement reduction from the sensitivity estimate, likely enough to pass T=4.5mm without large oversizing. Stays well within [1,14].

No oracle data at R0=4mm. Sensitivity -0.359 mm/mm measured at R=6–8mm. R=8mm is within domain, above the failing R=4mm, at the high end of the sensitivity range — likely satisfies 3.8mm cap. Result enables binary search down (pass) or up (fail) in one more solve.

At R=8 displacement is 4.282 mm, 0.482 mm above target. Sensitivity at R=6 is −0.359 mm/mm; at R=8 the response is shallower (~−0.25 mm/mm estimated). Linear correction: ΔR≈1.9 mm → R≈10. Adding margin for nonlinear roll-off gives R=11, within [1,14].

No FEA data yet. Sensitivity of -0.359 mm/mm measured at R=6 suggests each mm of rib height reduces displacement by ~0.36 mm. R=4 fails; jumping to R=8 (center of the useful stiffening range, 4 mm above R0) is a well-targeted first probe: it sits squarely in the neighbourhood where the sensitivity was measured and should land near or below the 3.8 mm threshold without over-building.

At R=8 the displacement is 4.282 mm, needing a reduction of ~0.48 mm. The sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm; assuming it weakens somewhat at higher R (diminishing returns), a +2 mm step to R=10 is estimated to yield ~3.56 mm, comfortably below 3.8 mm without grossly oversizing. R=10 stays well within the [1,14] domain.

Local sensitivity from the R=8→10 interval is −0.217 mm/mm. At R=10 the deficit is 3.847−3.8=0.047 mm, requiring only ~0.22 mm more. R=11 adds 1 mm of margin to account for the non-linearity of the stiffness response (the curve flattens as ribs grow taller) while staying well inside the [1,14] domain and avoiding unnecessary oversizing.

Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm. R=4 fails; estimated displacement ~4.5–5 mm. Threshold crossing is near R=6–7 mm. Adding 1 mm margin for nonlinear flattening gives R=8 mm: likely passes on first solve without excessive oversizing.

At R=8 mm, displacement=4.282 mm; need -0.48 mm. Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm; diminishing returns expected at R=8, so linear ΔR≈1.34 mm undershoots. R=10 mm is a one-step conservative bet without excessive oversizing.

Linear interpolation on the two bracketing solves (R=8→4.282 mm, R=10→3.847 mm) yields a local slope of -0.217 mm/mm. From R=10, the remaining deficit is 3.847-3.8=0.047 mm, requiring ΔR≈0.22 mm. R=10.5 provides a small margin above the minimum estimate while staying well within the [1,14] mm domain and avoiding oversizing.

Using the sensitivity d(u)/d(R) = -0.359 mm/mm at R=6 and a 1/R scaling model: d(R) ~ C/R. Fitting d'(6) = -C/36 = -0.359 gives C ≈ 12.9, so d(2) ≈ 6.5 mm (consistent with failure) and the threshold 3.9 mm is crossed near R ≈ 3.3 mm. R=5 mm gives a comfortable margin above that crossover while remaining well below the domain ceiling, minimising oversizing.

R=5→5.507mm, need 3.9mm, deficit=1.607mm. Sensitivity -0.359mm/mm at R=6 gives linear estimate ΔR≈4.5mm→R≈9.5mm. Stiffness grows super-linearly with rib height, so true sensitivity strengthens; R=9mm discounts slightly for nonlinearity without oversizing.

R=9mm gives 4.049mm; need 0.15mm more reduction. Sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm; curve flattens at higher R (~-0.25 mm/mm near R=9). Delta R = 0.15/0.28 ≈ 0.5mm → R≈9.5, rounded to 10mm for a small safety margin without oversizing.

No FEA data yet. R=2 fails; domain is [1,14]. The sensitivity at R=6 is -0.359 mm/mm, so we expect meaningful stiffening as R grows. Choosing R=8 sits in the upper-middle of the domain, likely clearing the 3.9 mm threshold while leaving headroom to back off if the true response is less stiff than the linear estimate suggests.

At R=8 displacement is 4.281 mm, need –0.381 mm. Measured sensitivity –0.359 mm/mm is at R=6–8; it diminishes with R (stiffness ∝ R^3). Naive linear step would be +1 mm, but with decreasing sensitivity a +2 mm step to R=10 provides margin without large oversizing, staying well within [1,14].

No measured displacement exists yet. The sensitivity is calibrated at R = 6 mm, making it the most informative first solve: the result will both reveal the actual displacement at that point and let me use the local gradient to extrapolate toward the 3.9 mm target in the next step, rather than guessing blind from an uncalibrated region.
At R=6 mm displacement=4.999 mm, target=3.9 mm. Gap=1.099 mm. Sensitivity=-0.3586 mm/mm → dR=1.099/0.3586≈3.1 mm. R=6+3.1≈9.1, rounded to 9 mm to stay conservative within the allowed domain.

At R=9 displacement=4.049, need 0.149 mm more reduction. Average sensitivity R=6→9 is -0.317 mm/mm (diminishing from -0.359). Local sensitivity at R=9 is ~-0.25 to -0.28 mm/mm. A +2 mm step to R=11 yields ~0.5-0.6 mm additional reduction, landing near 3.5 mm — comfortably under 3.9 mm without gross oversizing.

geoNotes: 19/19 unit tests pass (ribbed-geometry_test.ts). deno check and deno fmt clean on all three new files.
deno.json: two new modules added to the check task (ribbed-geometry.ts, solve-one-ribs.ts) and experiment:solve-one-ribs task added with identical permissions to experiment:solve-one.

u(2)/u(12) ≈ 2.22 — clear stiffening signal. Von Mises is slightly higher at R=12 (17.1 vs 16.0 MPa): stiffer ribs redirect the load path through the T-section leg, concentrating bending stress near the fixed wall. No single-variable textbook formula predicts this ratio for five discrete ribs on a finite plate — the geometry satisfies the experiment design intent.

build123d script uses direct algebra: Box + Box.move(Location(...)) performs boolean union in build123d algebra mode, producing a single fused solid for Gmsh meshing. Each of the 6 Box() calls is unrolled (not looped) for determinism and testability.
